summary: M1 PASS_SCOPED. M2 IN_PROGRESS. Bridge current HEAD 50978189950cd36cdae6ea4e19f87006ce1aa1d5 passed full CI+DB validation. Lite current-head Runner safety-contract, Playwright E2E and cross-browser passed; normal CI is blocked solely by npm audit (11 findings: 3 low, 8 moderate, 0 high/critical), including upstream deepmerge@4.3.1 with no patched npm release. Plus current-head normal CI passed; Playwright E2E is still in progress. All PRs remain Draft; no deploy, merge, live dispatch or mathematical certification. evidence_rule: Si un comentario de PR cita un SHA o una prueba más nueva, esa evidencia manda y este archivo debe actualizarse en el mismo cambio.

audience.executes_this_roadmap: Un LLM/agente consumidor puede completar tareas autorizadas sin acceso GitHub mediante Observer y/o Bridge. La implementación/mantenimiento del plano auxiliar puede requerir un agente mantenedor con permisos GitHub separados.
audience.does_not_execute_this_roadmap: No se limita el agente consumidor a Observer: puede entrar por Bridge directamente o combinar Observer y Bridge.

steps: No solicitar, copiar, registrar ni hacer commit de secretos: llm, SERVICE_API_KEY, GITHUB_READ_TOKEN, GH_TOKEN, SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY o BRIDGE_ADMIN_PASSWORD.
Usar GitHub como fuente de verdad; verificar refs, PR heads, despliegues y evidencia de workflows actuales antes de depender de SHAs históricos.
El LLM autorizado puede entrar por Observer, Bridge o una ruta híbrida; en el acceso directo Bridge consulta Observer internamente para contexto/política.
Observer entrega contexto/política; Bridge autentica y persiste comandos tipados/idempotentes; el Runner dentro de Actions será el ejecutor de M2 (aún no implementado).

El usuario ya concedió autonomía general para completar el trabajo ordinario dentro del alcance, repositorios, gates, workflows, ramas y límites establecidos. No pedir aprobación por cada despacho, prueba, reconciliación o bloque rutinario.
Ejecutar automáticamente consultas, correcciones, pruebas, despachos y reconciliaciones ordinarias cuando contratos, allowlists, scopes y pruebas demuestren que están dentro de política.

Escalar únicamente decisiones materiales no resueltas por documentación/pruebas: cambios de alcance, criterios ambiguos, licencia, exposición de datos, aceptación de riesgo nuevo o desactivación de protecciones.
Un fallo técnico ordinario se investiga, corrige y vuelve a probar sin pedir permiso. Si no existe camino seguro definido, detener solo la operación afectada y explicar el bloqueo concreto.
No crear un mecanismo externo de aprobación por evento. Fortalecer las pruebas automatizadas como fuente de verdad operativa.
Registrar request/correlation/validation IDs, fingerprint idempotente, receipt UUID, Actions run ID, Runner record, SHA y conclusión observada. Nunca registrar credenciales.

design_decision.name: multi-entry multi-transport command plane
design_decision.objective: Permitir que distintos LLM/agentes completen las operaciones del prompt Precision Lab —lectura, diagnóstico, patch, pruebas, commits/PR, certificación, reconciliación y continuidad— sin que el LLM necesite credenciales ni acceso directo a GitHub.
design_decision.architecture: LLM/Agent → (Observer OR Bridge OR Observer+Bridge) → Bridge Command API → existing Runner execution plane → Lite/Plus. En la ruta Bridge directa, Bridge consulta Observer internamente para contexto, estado canónico y política. Evidencia retorna por Runner → Bridge receipt → requester; Observer puede ofrecer la misma lectura.

component_roles.observer: Plano de información y política: estado bilateral, branches/HEAD, lectura de archivos/repositorio, continuidad, planes, evidencia y evaluación de bloqueos. No ejecuta commits ni mantiene la idempotencia transaccional de comandos.
component_roles.bridge: Puerta multiagente y plano de comandos: identidades/scopes por agente, contrato tipado, validación final, durable idempotency, queue/lease, receipts, coordinación/reconciliación. Las entradas directas deben consultar Observer internamente para contexto/política live.
component_roles.runner: Plano de ejecución dentro de GitHub Actions en Lite/Plus. Conserva certification-runner.yml para gates y añade capacidad controlada de repo changes, tests, commits/PR y callback. No es una API pública LLM ni un segundo servicio Runner.

routes.use: Agentes que prefieren API/OpenAPI de Observer para lectura, contexto, planificación y delegación.

routes.route: LLM → Bridge → (Observer internal context/policy) → Runner → Lite/Plus
routes.use: Agentes que pueden hacer REST/MCP/SDK/CLI directamente a Bridge; no requieren llamar Observer por separado.

routes.route: LLM → Observer (GET context/plan) + LLM → Bridge (POST command)
routes.use: Agentes que prefieren separar lectura y escritura.

routes.route: LLM with delegated GitHub access → GitHub Actions/Runner
routes.use: Excepción opcional para agentes con GitHub autorizado; no es requisito para el sistema sin GitHub.

credential_boundaries: LLM → Observer: per-agent read/API identity; no GitHub credential.
LLM → Bridge: per-agent key with context:read, command:submit and/or command:read scopes; no dispatch/admin secrets.
Bridge → Observer: dedicated internal service identity, proposed OBSERVER_BASE_URL + OBSERVER_SERVICE_KEY, server-only.
Bridge → GitHub Actions: dispatch-only token, server-only.
Runner → Bridge: GitHub OIDC workload identity or short-lived one-time lease token for task claim/result callback.
Runner → GitHub repository: repo-scoped workflow permissions/secrets; never exposed to LLM.
not_in_scope: Giving LLMs GitHub PATs, Supabase credentials, Bridge admin credentials or server-to-server secrets.
Arbitrary remote shell execution or arbitrary workflow names/refs/targets supplied by LLM.
A new public Runner service or duplicated planning/idempotency engines.
A route that trusts LLM-supplied RUN decision, branch/SHA or certification PASS.

autonomy.authorization: General autonomous execution within existing delegated Precision Lab scope, repositories, canonical branches, gates and policies.
autonomy.routine_operations: No human approval per routine command, test, dispatch or reconciliation when schema, allowlists, scopes and tests establish the operation is permitted.
escalation: License, publication, data exposure or new risk decisions
Disabling an established protection or undefined product behavior
autonomy.outcome_unknown: Reconcile by the same idempotency key; never blind retry.

invariants: LLMs may connect to Observer, Bridge directly, or both; Observer is not a mandatory hop for every agent.
Bridge direct requests must internally obtain live context/policy from Observer before any repository mutation or certification dispatch.
Observer remains the source of truth for state, repository context, canonical branch/SHA, planning and evidence.
Bridge owns command validation, agent scopes, durable idempotency, queue/lease, receipts and dispatch coordination.
Runner is the only execution plane for repository changes and certification workflows; no public Runner API or second Runner service.
LLMs never receive GitHub write credentials, Supabase credentials, Bridge admin credentials or server-to-server secrets.
Only allowlisted typed repository operations and named test profiles may execute; no arbitrary remote shell.
Every mutation verifies target repository, canonical/policy-approved branch and expected SHA; stale SHA causes conflict and reconciliation.
Same idempotency key and fingerprint return the same command/receipt; payload conflict is rejected; uncertain outcomes are reconciled, never blindly retried.
Correlation/validation IDs, actor identity, command ID, receipt UUID, Actions run ID, Runner record, SHA and output are traceable.
GitHub Actions SUCCESS, command completed, test PASS and mathematical certification PASS remain distinct states.
Existing A/B Observer→Bridge read tests remain closed and are not repeated absent invalidating changes.
Routine operations inside delegated scope need no human approval per event; escalate material unresolved decisions.
Keep existing certification-runner.yml as gate executor; any repository worker workflow is an entrypoint in the same Runner execution plane, not a second Runner service.
Command completion is observed by pull only: an agent without an inbound endpoint reads GET /api/v1/commands/{command_id} or lookup by Idempotency-Key. Bridge never pushes results to LLMs.

Self-declared LLM capabilities and results from a consumer's own sandbox are hypotheses or local checks. Only a per-consumer probe against Bridge or Observer using that consumer's own key, and allowlisted Runner profiles, count as evidence.

A consumer holding any write-capable connector (GitHub, Render or other) must not write to canonical branches or to infrastructure outside Bridge. Agents that use Bridge may hold such connectors only for read-only use, or for non-canonical work authorized under the same branch, expected_sha and evidence rules. Such consumers are not credentialless for M6.

phases.title: Extend existing Runner execution plane for repository changes
steps: Worker entrypoints workflow_dispatch-only añadidos a Lite y Plus; conservan certification-runner.yml y reciben únicamente command_id opaco.
Bridge valida GitHub OIDC (issuer, firma, audience, repositorio/ID, workflow, evento, rama y run) y vincula el run a un lease durable de 60 minutos con límite de intentos.
Worker recupera un manifiesto tipado, valida propietario/fingerprint/target/branch/expected_sha y aplica create/replace/delete seguros sobre agent/{command_id} con CAS y blob-SHA.
Perfiles allowlisted ejecutan validaciones fijas. Plus unit instala frontend con npm ci y ejecuta backend pytest más frontend npm test; frontend lockfile sincronizado.
Cambios validados generan commit y draft PR sin auto-merge; callback OIDC + lease persiste status, Actions run, commit y PR; replay/reconciliación no redispatcha ciegamente.
Completar checks normales sobre SHA exactos de Lite/Plus y resolver el hard gate npm audit de Lite sin reducir la política.
La aceptación M2 requiere una traza end-to-end autorizada Bridge → Actions → Runner → receipt → Observer y replay idempotente; no se ha ejecutado.
phases.exit_criteria: A typed repo patch sent by a no-GitHub agent produces a validated commit/PR and evidence without direct GitHub credentials in the agent.

phases.title: Certify multi-agent, multi-transport end-to-end operation
steps: Use two distinct LLM agents and at least two transport mechanisms with no GitHub credentials supplied to either agent.
Read canonical state and source files, identify a real authorized correction, submit patch, run validations, obtain commit/PR and reconcile.
Exercise 401/403, stale SHA, policy WAIT/REUSE, payload conflict, exact replay, concurrency, timeout and callback failure.
Prove there is no duplicate workflow and complete trace request→command→receipt→Actions→Runner→commit/PR→test evidence.
phases.exit_criteria: Two distinct agents and two transports complete the same authorized repository-change workflow using only their own Observer/Bridge credentials; the trace is complete and replay creates no duplicate.

phases.title: Freeze auxiliary infrastructure and resume mathematical certification
steps: Publish evidence and capability/transport limitations.
Freeze auxiliary Observer/Bridge/adapter scope; do not add cosmetic features.
Resume Lite/Plus certification from canonical current_state/continuity without repeating valid mathematical evidence.
phases.exit_criteria: Multi-agent access and repository change capability are proven; remaining work returns to the mathematical certification objectives.

do_not: Do not give LLMs GitHub write tokens, Supabase credentials, Bridge admin secrets or internal service keys.
Do not make Observer the mandatory network hop for every agent; support direct Bridge and hybrid routes under the same policy.
Do not let Bridge direct requests bypass live Observer context/policy validation.
Do not create a second Runner service or duplicate policy/planning/idempotency logic; a worker workflow may be an entrypoint in the same Runner execution plane.
Do not expose a public unauthenticated Runner API.
Do not execute arbitrary shell commands, arbitrary workflow names/refs, unbounded patches or unrestricted repository paths supplied by the LLM.
Do not force-push or overwrite canonical/protected branches; require expected_sha and isolated work branches.
Do not retry an uncertain POST blindly; reconcile by the original idempotency key.
Do not confuse command acceptance, workflow SUCCESS, test PASS and mathematical certification PASS.
Do not reopen phases A/B or repeat their read-only tests unless a code/contract change invalidates the evidence.
Do not require human approval per routine operation already within delegated policy; escalate material unresolved decisions only.
Do not merge PR, deploy production, rotate/revoke production credentials or change production routing as a side effect of this documentation decision.
Do not add GraphQL, gRPC, raw TCP/SSH, Git transports, WebSocket command channels, voice/realtime, or browser/computer-use paths to the command plane.
Do not count a consumer's sandbox tests, generated specs or curl results as Lite/Plus validation or as proof of access to Observer or Bridge.
Do not assign a consumer a route from its self-description; assign it only after its consumer probe.
Do not let sub-agents of a single platform stand in for two independent agents in M6 acceptance.
Do not count a consumer with write-capable connectors (GitHub, Render or others) as credentialless for M6 while those connectors are connected.

definition_of_done.adapter_scope: M5 adapter selection may be phased by concrete LLM/provider demand; P0/P1 and two distinct transport paths are required for multi-agent acceptance.
definition_of_done.merge_gate_not_a_substitute: CI/PR review is code evidence, not live interoperability proof. No GitHub credential is supplied to the test LLMs.
definition_of_done.acceptance: At least two different LLM agents and two different connection mechanisms complete read→diagnose→patch→validate→commit/PR→reconcile with a full evidence chain and exact idempotent replay.
definition_of_done.preserve: A/B are already completed and are not repeated. Historical O1–O7 evidence remains stored under legacy_observer_only_phases.
definition_of_done.after_done: Freeze auxiliary multi-agent infrastructure and resume mathematical certification Lite/Plus; agents continue routine work within the proven policy.

evidence_classification.sandbox_probe_detail: Public curl to api.github.com without credentials, validation of a sample OpenAPI 3.0.3 spec, and urllib/https requests to public endpoints. These prove outbound HTTPS from the sandbox only.

llm_mechanism_review_2026_10_31.verdict: The v2 architecture does not change. Most reports say they cannot call an arbitrary REST API, MCP server or webhook on their own, so the practical bottleneck is the host adapter per deployment, not the Command API. Routes are assigned per consumer after probing.
findings: Function Calling is named as a consumer's own mechanism in 5 of 6 reports, but every report conditions it on the host exposing the tool. It is the first adapter to build in M4, generated from the same OpenAPI document.
No agent without a public endpoint can receive inbound notifications, so command outcomes are read by pull (GET by command_id or lookup by Idempotency-Key).
Consumer sandboxes can run local checks and generate patches, but their results are never validation evidence for Lite/Plus.

A consumer holding write-capable connectors (GitHub, Render or others) could write outside Bridge. The exception must cover every write-capable connector, not only GitHub, and such consumers do not count as credentialless for M6.

The roadmap does not define a background process that closes abandoned accepted/queued commands or expired leases without a receipt. Bridge tests cover lease expiry at claim time only. This must be designed before M2 closes.

roadmap_adjustments: Consumer probe: each LLM that connects uses its own key. Battery: docs/parallel-tool-consumer-probe-battery.md (33 tests, groups A to F). Checks include GET /api/v1/capabilities and GET /api/v1/context/status with context:read (200); POST without command:submit (403); POST with command:submit (202); exact replay (200); GET by command_id and lookup. Record result per mechanism and per consumer. Status: PENDING until Bridge to Observer is deployed and configured.
Routes are assigned per consumer from probe results, not from a global design. A consumer without outbound HTTP uses an adapter or the hybrid route.
Function Calling adapter (M4): generate tool schemas from the same OpenAPI document and from GET /api/v1/capabilities. Do not maintain separate hand-written schemas.

Connector exception: any connector with write capability (GitHub, Render or other) is inventoried per consumer and never writes to canonical branches or to infrastructure outside Bridge. A consumer that uses Bridge may hold such connectors only for read-only work, unless a non-canonical workflow is separately authorized under the same branch, expected_sha and evidence rules. A consumer with write-capable connectors is not credentialless for M6 and must disconnect them during the M6 test, with the disconnection recorded.
Add a Bridge background sweep for accepted/queued commands without receipt and for expired leases, moving them to reconcile_required without redispatch. Design and test before M2 closes.
M6 uses two independent consumers, each with its own key and host. Sub-agents of one platform do not count.
open_items: Identify the host runtime of each consumer LLM; the reports do not state it and cannot be assumed.
Confirm the design of the background sweep (schedule, lease expiry window, reconcile_required transition).
Run the consumer probe after OBSERVER_SERVICE_KEY is configured and the Bridge build is deployed. Until then no route is assigned to any consumer.
